title: The Public Bench
fact_notes: オリジナル教材。人物、出来事は架空の例。実在の調査、実証結果、制度、個別医療の助言ではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A town council in an imagined community receives several requests to install new benches near a busy shopping street.
sentences.ja: 架空の地域の町議会は混雑する商店街近くに新しいベンチを設置する複数の依頼を受ける。

sentences.en: The officials initially plan to place all of the benches in locations that are most visible from the entrances to popular shops.
sentences.ja: 職員は当初人気店入口から最も見えやすい場所に全ベンチを置く計画を立てる。

sentences.en: They believe that visitors will appreciate having somewhere to rest after completing their purchases.
sentences.ja: 訪問者が買物後に休む場所があることをありがたく思うと考える。

sentences.en: A resident questions whether the proposed locations would also serve people who have difficulty walking long distances.
sentences.ja: 住民は提案場所が長距離歩行に困難を抱える人にも役立つか疑問に思う。

sentences.en: The council begins examining the street as a route rather than simply as a collection of destinations.
sentences.ja: 議会は通りを目的地の集合としてだけでなく経路として調べ始める。

sentences.en: Someone who needs frequent opportunities to rest may find a bench particularly useful halfway between two places, even if that location attracts relatively few visitors.
sentences.ja: 頻繁に休憩する機会を必要とする人にとって、比較的訪問者が少なくても二地点の中間のベンチが特に役立つかもしれない。

sentences.en: A bench located close to another available seat might serve a different purpose from one placed along a long section of pavement without any resting place.
sentences.ja: 他の利用可能席の近くのベンチは休憩場所のない長い歩道区間のものと異なる目的に役立つかもしれない。

sentences.en: The officials recognize that the total number of seats cannot by itself describe the accessibility of an entire journey.
sentences.ja: 席の総数だけでは移動全体の利用しやすさを記述できないと認識する。

sentences.en: They consult several hypothetical users whose reasons for visiting the street differ.
sentences.ja: 訪問理由が異なる複数の仮想利用者に相談する。

sentences.en: Some would prefer sheltered seats near particular destinations, whereas others value the opportunity to pause at regular intervals during a journey.
sentences.ja: 特定目的地の近くの屋根付き席を好む人もいれば移動中定期的に休む機会を重視する人もいる。

sentences.en: The council considers whether several arrangements might address different needs while remaining within the available budget.
sentences.ja: 利用可能予算内で異なる必要に対応する複数の配置があり得るか検討する。

sentences.en: It also recognizes that the choice of locations must consider practical requirements involving safety and the use of public space.
sentences.ja: 場所選択では安全と公共空間利用に関する実務要件も考慮すべきと認識する。

sentences.en: Instead of evaluating the proposal exclusively through the number of people sitting on new benches, the officials discuss which journeys the benches would make easier to complete.
sentences.ja: 新ベンチに座る人数だけで提案を評価せず、どの移動がベンチによって完了しやすくなるか議論する。

sentences.en: A seat that is occupied infrequently may still provide an important opportunity for someone who could not otherwise reach a particular destination.
sentences.ja: 利用頻度が低い席でもそうでなければ目的地に着けない人に重要な機会を提供し得る。

sentences.en: The fictional discussion does not establish how actual streets should be designed or managed.
sentences.ja: 架空議論は現実の通りの設計・管理法を確定しない。

sentences.en: It illustrates how different definitions of public benefit can influence the location of an everyday resource.
sentences.ja: 公共利益の異なる定義が日常資源の位置にどう影響するかを示す。

sentences.en: Providing the same number of facilities does not necessarily create the same opportunities for every person.
sentences.ja: 同数の施設提供は必ずしも全員に同じ機会を生まない。

sentences.en: An assessment of public services may require attention to the relationships between resources and the activities they are intended to support.
sentences.ja: 公共サービス評価には資源と支援対象活動の関係への注意が必要かもしれない。

sentences.en: The placement of a simple bench can reveal questions about whose needs are considered when public decisions are made.
sentences.ja: 単純なベンチの配置は公的判断時に誰の必要が考慮されるかという問いを明らかにし得る。

sentences.en: Meaningful access depends not only on what exists but also on whether people can make use of it when they need it.
sentences.ja: 意味あるアクセスは存在する物だけでなく必要時に利用できるかにも依存する。

vocabulary.definition: state of being hard to do
in the middle of a distance
quality of being easy to reach
places or equipment provided for use
act of putting in a location

questions.prompt: What does the council initially plan to install?
options: New traffic lights at every school.

questions.prompt: What concern does the resident raise?
options: Benches are never useful to shoppers.
The council has already removed all benches.
The chosen locations may not help people who struggle to walk far.
questions.explanation_ja: 長距離歩行の困難への配慮。

questions.prompt: Why view the street as a route?
options: Resting opportunities along the journey may matter more than proximity to shops alone.
Every user travels to the same shop.
Only the street's total length is important.
The benches must be located at the endpoints.

questions.prompt: What does the seat count fail to describe by itself?
What differences do the hypothetical users express?
options: Preferences for sheltered seats or regular resting intervals.
A wish to remove all public space.
Every user needs the exact same seats.
Different needs may be addressed within practical constraints.

questions.prompt: Why can an infrequently occupied seat still matter?
options: It necessarily wastes every public resource.
It guarantees that nobody will need rest.
It may enable a journey that would otherwise be difficult or impossible.
Its value depends solely on being occupied continuously.
questions.explanation_ja: 利用可能性が移動を支える。

questions.prompt: What does the example not establish?
options: The possibility of differing public benefits.
A design rule for an actual street.
questions.explanation_ja: 実際の設計法を確立しない。

options: The act of putting something in a particular location.

questions.prompt: Which statement best expresses the argument?
options: Public resources should be evaluated in relation to the opportunities they enable for different users.
The most frequently occupied facility always has the greatest public value.
Equal numbers of seats guarantee equal opportunities.
Every bench should be placed only near a shop entrance.
questions.explanation_ja: 利用者の機会を考慮する。

grammar.focus: whether the proposed locations would also serve
even if that location attracts relatively few visitors

grammar.explanation_ja: who節がsomeoneを修飾、otherwiseはそうでなければ。

paraphrases.source: A resident questions whether the proposed locations would also serve people who have difficulty walking long distances.
paraphrases.rewrite: The resident asks whether the chosen sites would be useful for people who struggle to walk far.

paraphrases.source: Someone who needs frequent opportunities to rest may find a bench particularly useful halfway between two places, even if that location attracts relatively few visitors.
paraphrases.rewrite: A halfway seat can matter even when few people visit that area.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 利用者数だけではない価値。

paraphrases.source: Some would prefer sheltered seats near particular destinations, whereas others value the opportunity to pause at regular intervals during a journey.
paraphrases.rewrite: Some users prefer sheltered seats while others need regular opportunities to rest.

paraphrases.source: A seat that is occupied infrequently may still provide an important opportunity for someone who could not otherwise reach a particular destination.
paraphrases.rewrite: Even a seldom-used seat could allow someone to reach a destination.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 目的地に到達する支援。

discourse.role_ja: 目的地でなく移動経路。
人数でなく可能になる移動へ。
存在に加えて利用可能性を論じる。

cloze.explanation_ja: 屋根などで守られた席。
